title: Meter aggregation mismatch causing incorrect throttles and billing divergence
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Several customers and internal billing checks show divergence between token metering and enforced throttles for composite request keys (org+route+api-key). Symptoms include unexpected 429 throttles while usage counters report remaining quota, and invoice line-items that undercount generated tokens for specific routes. The root cause appears related to how the policy engine aggregates short-lived request batches and applies smoothing windows when keys are sharded across multiple enforcement workers.

Observed behavior:
- Multiple customers reported 429s at peak that do not correlate to quota exhaustion in the billing ledger.
- The cost reconciliation job (billing-recon) shows a subset of generated tokens missing for routes that use composite-key grouping (e.g., org:ACME + route:/chat/completions + key:k_abcd).
- Grafana dashboards show enforcement decisions (throttle/allow) mismatching meter increments by ~1.3% on the affected routes during high concurrency windows (see links).

Steps to reproduce (dev env):
1) Spin up local policy worker set with sharding enabled (WORKER_SHARDS=4) and smoothing window = 250ms.
2) Send 500 concurrent requests using the composite key header across 4 client senders with inter-request jitter.
3) Observe enforcement logs and billing local ledger.
4) Compare enforcement decisions with meter increments (billing-recon dry run).

Key logs (sanitized):
- enforcement-worker-2 INFO [2026-02-24T18:12:03Z] decision=THROTTLE key=org:ACME|route:/chat/completions|k_abcd window_ms=250 shard=2
- meter-aggregator INFO [2026-02-24T18:12:03Z] incremented key=org:ACME|route:/chat/completions|k_abcd tokens=24 batch_id=0x7f3 shard=3
- billing-proxy WARN [2026-02-24T18:12:04Z] reconcile-mismatch key=org:ACME|route:/chat/completions|k_abcd enforcement=throttle ledger_remaining=820

Hypotheses considered:
- H1: Race between aggregator flush and enforcement decision path due to non-atomic peer-to-peer increment across shards.
- H2: Off-by-one rounding when smoothing window overlaps bucket boundaries; increments get credited to the wrong time window and enforcement reads stale counters.
- H3: Shadow auth keys (legacy migration code) cause requests to be attributed to a different composite key at enforcement time (rare).

Experiments & findings:
- Reproduced locally with WORKER_SHARDS=4 and smoothing window >=200ms; mismatch frequency increases with more shards and larger window.
- Forcing atomic cross-shard reads (temporary patch) reduces mismatch to <0.05% in synthetic load.
- Disabling smoothing window eliminates the mismatch but causes higher burst throttling (bad for latency).

Immediate mitigation (hotfix):
- Deploy patch that aligns aggregator flush boundaries to enforcement read boundaries (hotfix branch: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/PR-5234). This reduces mismatch without disabling smoothing.
- Add a reconciliation alert (high severity) to detect divergence >0.5% between enforcement-decisions and meter-ack counts per-route per-org.

Temporary customer workarounds:
- For customers impacted, we can pin them to single-shard enforcement by setting POLICY_HINT=single-shard for their org until the release is rolled. Ops has a runbook for this (link below).

Planned remediation & follow-ups:
- Implement atomic cross-shard increment using a lightweight consensus step or central aggregator (design doc: Drive link).
- Add unit/integration tests to simulate interleaved aggregator/enforcer timing and verify zero divergence for window sizes in [50ms, 500ms].
- Add e2e billing-recon smoke test in CI for composite-key routes.
- Postmortem and customer communication draft.

Acceptance criteria:
- Reconciliation divergence reduced to <0.1% on synthetic and prod sampling.
- No customer reports of unexpected 429s traced to aggregation mismatch for 14 days after release.
- CI tests exercising shard-counts 1..8 pass deterministically.

Notes / Links:
- PR (hotfix): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5234
- Design doc (implementation options): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/REDWOOD_BILLING_DESIGNS
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood-internal.com/d/rate-limiter/meter-enforcement-divergence
- Billing recon job: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/tree/main/recon

Next actions:
- Miguel: continue hotfix rollout to staging and run 24h smoke with real traffic replay (estimate 1 day).
- Asha: prepare customer comms list and draft apology/mitigation note (estimate 0.5 days).
- Infra: evaluate central aggregator TTL and failure modes (sync with SRE).
